entries.answer: An affix in Filipino is a prefix, an infix or a suffix added to a root, and the language uses them so heavily that learning it is mostly learning the affixes rather than the vocabulary. The infix is the unusual one, because inserting a syllable into the middle of a root is rare in the languages of the region, and the standard example is the insertion of pam in sumulat, where it marks the person who caused the writing: the root is sulat for writing, and the same root with other affixes gives a different actor, a different tense and a different object. The tense affixes are among the most regular part of the system, since a completed action, an ongoing one and a future one are all built from the root with a fixed marker, and a learner can therefore form a verb family from one word. The general principle is that the affix order is fixed and it is not the same as word order, which is the thing a beginner gets wrong first.
